Normalizing hpc_job_id STRING to compute_

attributes.name: demux_result_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to sequencing.demux_result. Business justification: Lineage events capture demultiplexing as a transformation step in data processing workflows. This link enables tracking FASTQ file generation and subsequent processing, required for GxP-compliant data

attributes.name: genome_assembly_id
attributes.description: Reference to the reference genome assembly used during alignment or variant calling (e.g., GRCh38, GRCh37/hg19, T2T-CHM13). Ensures traceability of genomic coordinates and reproducibility of variant calls across pipeline runs.

attributes.name: library_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to sequencing.library. Business justification: Lineage tracking at library level enables sample-level audit trails and consent management. This link supports clinical laboratories in demonstrating complete chain of custody from sample receipt thro

attributes.name: pipeline_run_step_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific pipeline run step that produced or triggered this lineage event. Links the lineage record to the bioinformatics pipeline execution context for reproducibility and audit traceability.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; GxP Good Practice Regulations; HIPAA

attributes.name: primary_data_genomic_artifact_id
attributes.description: Reference to the genomic data artifact (e.g., FASTQ, BAM, VCF, gVCF, annotation file) that served as the input to this transformation event. Supports forward and backward data lineage tracing.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy; GxP

attributes.name: sample_specimen_id
attributes.description: Reference to the biological sample associated with this lineage event, as tracked in the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS). Provides traceability from raw genomic data back to the originating sample.
attributes.references: ISO 15189; CLIA; CAP; HIPAA; LabVantage LIMS

attributes.name: sequencing_run_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to sequencing.sequencing_run. Business justification: Lineage events track transformations from sequencing runs through pipeline stages, required for GxP compliance and FDA 21 CFR Part 11 audit trails. This link enables complete data provenance from raw

attributes.name: target_artifact_genomic_artifact_id
attributes.description: Reference to the genomic data artifact produced as the output of this transformation event (e.g., aligned BAM, called VCF, annotated VCF, clinical report). Enables downstream lineage traversal.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy; GxP

attributes.name: algorithm_parameters
attributes.description: Serialized string (JSON or key=value pairs) of the runtime parameters passed to the bioinformatics tool for this transformation event (e.g., minimum base quality score, minimum mapping quality, ploidy setting). Critical for reproducibility and regulatory audit trails.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; GxP; NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy; ISO 13485

attributes.name: assay_type
attributes.description: Type of genomic assay associated with this lineage event, indicating the sequencing or array methodology applied (e.g., Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS), Whole Exome Sequencing (WES), targeted gene panel, SNP array, Copy Number Variation (CNV) analysis, RNA-seq, amplicon sequencing). Used for assay-specific pipeline routing and regulatory classification. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: WGS|WES|targeted_panel|SNP_array|CNV_analysis|RNA_seq|amplicon — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: FDA IVD Regulations; CLIA; CAP; ISO 13485; IVDR 2017/746

attributes.name: compute_platform
attributes.description: The computing infrastructure platform on which this transformation event was executed (e.g., AWS Batch, AWS EMR, HPC SLURM cluster, Databricks). Used for cost attribution, performance benchmarking, and infrastructure capacity planning. attributes.name: cpu_cores_used
attributes.description: Number of CPU cores allocated and consumed by the compute job executing this transformation event. Used for HPC/cloud resource consumption tracking, cost attribution, and pipeline performance optimization.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) when this lineage event record was first captured in the data platform. Distinct from event_timestamp (the real-world transformation time). Required for GxP audit trails and 21 CFR Part 11 record integrity.

attributes.name: error_code
attributes.description: Structured error or exception code returned by the bioinformatics tool or pipeline orchestrator when a transformation event fails (e.g., TOOL_EXIT_NONZERO, INSUFFICIENT_COVERAGE, CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, TIMEOUT). Used for failure root-cause analysis and automated alerting.

attributes.name: error_message
attributes.description: Human-readable error or exception message captured when a transformation event fails or produces a warning. Provides detailed context for failure root-cause analysis, pipeline debugging, and GxP deviation investigation.

attributes.name: event_code
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for this lineage event, formatted as LIN- followed by an alphanumeric code. Used for cross-system referencing, audit log correlation, and regulatory submission traceability.

attributes.name: event_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the data transformation event. Indicates whether the transformation is pending execution, actively running, successfully completed, failed with error, skipped due to conditional logic, or retried after a prior failure. Used for pipeline monitoring and failure root-cause analysis.

attributes.name: event_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) at which the data transformation event occurred in the bioinformatics pipeline. This is the principal real-world event time, distinct from record audit timestamps. Critical for GxP audit trails and 21 CFR Part 11 compliance.

attributes.name: event_type
attributes.description: Categorical discriminator identifying the kind of data transformation that occurred in the bioinformatics pipeline. Values: ingest (raw FASTQ ingestion), transform (alignment/variant calling), filter (QC filtering), merge (combining artifacts), split (demultiplexing), annotate (variant annotation), export (clinical report generation), archive (long-term storage). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ingest|transform|filter|merge|split|annotate|export|archive — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; GxP; HIPAA; NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy

attributes.name: execution_duration_seconds
attributes.description: Wall-clock elapsed time in seconds for the transformation event to complete, from job start to job end. Used for pipeline performance benchmarking, Turnaround Time (TAT) analysis, and SLA monitoring.

attributes.name: gxp_audit_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this transformation event is subject to GxP (Good Practice Regulations including GMP, GLP, GCP) audit trail requirements (True = GxP-regulated event, False = non-regulated event). Used to filter events for regulatory audit reporting and inspection readiness.
attributes.references: GxP Good Practice Regulations; 21 CFR Part 11; FDA; EMA; ICH

attributes.name: hipaa_phi_involved
attributes.business_glossary_term: HIPAA Protected Health Information (PHI) Involved Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this transformation event processed or produced data containing Protected Health Information (PHI) as defined under HIPAA (True = PHI involved, False = no PHI). Used for HIPAA compliance reporting, data access controls, and breach risk assessment.
attributes.references: HIPAA Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act; 45 CFR Parts 160 and 164

attributes.name: input_record_count
attributes.description: Number of input records, reads, or variants consumed by this transformation event (e.g., number of FASTQ reads ingested, number of variants in input VCF). Used for data volume tracking, QC validation, and pipeline performance analysis.
attributes.references: GxP; 21 CFR Part 11; NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy

attributes.name: memory_used_gb
attributes.description: Amount of RAM in gigabytes consumed by the compute job executing this transformation event. Used for HPC/cloud resource consumption tracking, cost attribution, and pipeline performance optimization.

attributes.name: operator_identity
attributes.description: Username, service account name, or system identity (human user or automated pipeline agent) that initiated or executed this transformation event. Required for GxP audit trails, 21 CFR Part 11 electronic signature traceability, and HIPAA access accountability.

attributes.name: operator_type
attributes.description: Categorizes whether the transformation event was initiated by a human user, an automated bioinformatics pipeline, a system service account, or a scheduled job. Supports audit trail differentiation and compliance reporting under 21 CFR Part 11.

attributes.name: output_record_count
attributes.description: Number of output records, reads, or variants produced by this transformation event (e.g., number of aligned reads in output BAM, number of variants in output VCF). Used for data volume tracking, QC validation, and yield analysis.
attributes.references: GxP; 21 CFR Part 11; NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy

attributes.name: pipeline_stage
attributes.description: High-level stage of the bioinformatics processing pipeline in which this transformation event occurred. Values: ingestion (raw FASTQ intake), preprocessing (trimming/QC), alignment (BAM/CRAM generation), variant_calling (VCF/gVCF), annotation (variant annotation), qc_filtering (QC-based filtering), reporting (clinical report generation), archival (long-term storage). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: ingestion|preprocessing|alignment|variant_calling|annotation|qc_filtering|reporting|archival — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: GxP; 21 CFR Part 11; CLIA; CAP; ISO 13485

attributes.name: qc_metric_name
attributes.description: Name of the primary Quality Control (QC) metric evaluated at this transformation step (e.g., mean_coverage_depth, percent_mapped_reads, phred_score_q30_percent, ts_tv_ratio, variant_call_rate). Provides context for the QC pass/fail determination.
attributes.references: ISO 13485; CLIA; CAP; GxP; Phred Score Standard

attributes.name: qc_metric_value
attributes.description: Numeric value of the primary Quality Control (QC) metric evaluated at this transformation step (e.g., 45.7 for mean coverage depth, 98.3 for percent mapped reads). Used for QC trending, threshold monitoring, and regulatory compliance reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 13485; CLIA; CAP; GxP; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: qc_pass_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the output artifact of this transformation event passed Quality Control (QC) criteria (True = QC passed, False = QC failed). Used for pipeline gating, clinical report eligibility, and regulatory compliance reporting.
attributes.references: ISO 13485; CLIA; CAP; GxP; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: retry_count
attributes.description: Number of times this transformation event has been retried following a prior failure. Used for pipeline reliability monitoring, failure pattern analysis, and identifying systemic infrastructure or data quality issues.

attributes.name: source_artifact_checksum
attributes.description: Cryptographic hash (MD5, SHA-256, or SHA-512) of the input genomic data artifact at the time of consumption. Used to verify data integrity, detect corruption, and confirm that the correct artifact version was used. Required for 21 CFR Part 11 and GxP data integrity compliance.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; GxP; ISO 13485; FDA Data Integrity Guidance

attributes.name: source_artifact_format
attributes.description: File format of the input genomic data artifact consumed by this transformation event (e.g., FASTQ for raw reads, BAM/CRAM for aligned reads, VCF/gVCF for variant calls). Enables format-aware lineage queries and pipeline validation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FASTQ|BAM|CRAM|VCF|gVCF|BED|FASTA|TSV|CSV|JSON|HTML|PDF — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: SAM/BAM Format Specification; VCF Specification v4.3; FASTQ Format Standard

attributes.name: source_artifact_path
attributes.description: Cloud or network storage path (e.g., S3 URI, ADLS path) of the input genomic data artifact consumed by this transformation event. Confidential as it may reveal internal infrastructure topology and data organization. Required for data recovery, re-processing, and audit traceability.

attributes.name: target_artifact_checksum
attributes.description: Cryptographic hash (MD5, SHA-256, or SHA-512) of the output genomic data artifact produced by this transformation event. Used to verify data integrity, detect corruption, and confirm artifact authenticity for downstream steps. Required for 21 CFR Part 11 and GxP data integrity compliance.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; GxP; ISO 13485; FDA Data Integrity Guidance

attributes.name: target_artifact_format
attributes.description: File format of the output genomic data artifact produced by this transformation event (e.g., BAM for alignment output, VCF for variant calling output, annotated VCF for annotation output). Enables format-aware lineage queries and downstream pipeline validation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FASTQ|BAM|CRAM|VCF|gVCF|BED|FASTA|TSV|CSV|JSON|HTML|PDF — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: SAM/BAM Format Specification; VCF Specification v4.3; FASTQ Format Standard

attributes.name: target_artifact_path
attributes.description: Cloud or network storage path (e.g., S3 URI, ADLS path) of the output genomic data artifact produced by this transformation event. Confidential as it may reveal internal infrastructure topology. Required for downstream pipeline steps, data recovery, and audit traceability.

attributes.name: tool_container_image
attributes.description: Docker or container image URI (including registry, repository, and digest/tag) used to execute the bioinformatics tool, ensuring exact computational environment reproducibility. Example: docker.io/broadinstitute/gatk:4.2.6.1. Supports GxP validation and 21 CFR Part 11 audit requirements.

attributes.name: tool_name
attributes.description: Name of the bioinformatics software tool or algorithm used to perform the data transformation (e.g., BWA-MEM, GATK HaplotypeCaller, STAR, Trimmomatic, SnpEff, VEP). Essential for reproducibility and regulatory validation documentation.

attributes.name: tool_version
attributes.description: Semantic version string of the bioinformatics tool used for the transformation (e.g., 4.2.6.1 for GATK, 0.7.17 for BWA). Required for reproducibility, pipeline validation, and regulatory submission documentation under GxP and 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; GxP; ISO 13485; ICH E6

attributes.name: updated_timestamp

attributes.name: use_classification
attributes.description: Regulatory use classification of the genomic data processed in this lineage event. Values: RUO (Research Use Only), IVD (In Vitro Diagnostic), LDT (Laboratory Developed Test), clinical_research, agricultural, pharmaceutical. Determines applicable regulatory framework and data handling requirements.

products.name: pipeline_validation_study
products.description: Master record of formal analytical validation studies conducted on bioinformatics pipelines for IVD/LDT regulatory compliance — including study name, pipeline version validated, assay type, validation type (analytical sensitivity, specificity, reproducibility, accuracy), study protocol reference, validation status (in-progress, passed, failed), LOD established, regulatory submission reference (FDA, CE-IVD), and validation completion date. attributes.name: minimum_phred_score

attributes.name: precision_cv_percent

attributes.description: The alternate (non-reference) allele nucleotide sequence observed at this locus. Stored in IUPAC nucleotide notation per VCF specification. Used for genotype call interpretation, allele frequency calculations, and pharmacogenomics classification.

attributes.name: ancestry_panel_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this SNP is designated as an Ancestry Informative Marker (AIM) in the genotyping panel design. attributes.description: Proportion of samples (or loci, depending on context) for which a confident genotype call was made at this SNP position, expressed as a decimal between 0 and 1. A key Quality Control (QC) metric for array-based genotyping; loci with call rate below threshold (e.g., <0.95) are typically excluded from downstream analysis.

attributes.name: call_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when the genotype call was computationally generated by the bioinformatics pipeline. Represents the principal business event timestamp for this result record. Stored in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset. Used for data lineage, audit trails, and TAT (Turnaround Time) calculations.

attributes.name: clinical_significance
attributes.description: Clinical significance classification of this SNP variant as reported in ClinVar or assigned by the clinical interpretation pipeline. Uses ACMG/AMP variant classification terminology. Applicable for clinical genomics and IVD assay workflows. Null for research-use-only (RUO) results without clinical interpretation.
attributes.references: ACMG/AMP Variant Classification Guidelines (Richards et al. 2015); ClinVar; FDA IVD Guidance; ISO 15189

attributes.name: coverage_depth
attributes.description: The number of sequencing reads covering this SNP locus (read depth / coverage depth) for sequencing-based genotyping. Null for array-based genotyping. A key QC metric; loci with coverage below threshold (e.g., <10x) may yield unreliable genotype calls. Used in WGS and WES workflows.
attributes.references: GATK Best Practices (Broad Institute); GA4GH; ISO 15189

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this SNP genotype result record was first created and persisted in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED timestamp for audit trail and data lineage purposes. Immutable after initial insert.

attributes.name: data_use_restriction
attributes.description: The data use restriction code governing permissible downstream uses of this genomic result, as defined by the GA4GH Data Use Ontology (DUO) and NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy. Values: GRU (General Research Use), HMB (Health/Medical/Biomedical), DS (Disease-Specific), POA (Population Origins/Ancestry), NRES (No Restrictions), no_restriction. Governs GWAS, pharmacogenomics, and agricultural genomics data sharing compliance.
attributes.references: NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy (GDS); GA4GH Data Use Ontology (DUO); GDPR Article 9; HIPAA 45 CFR Part 164

attributes.name: functional_consequence
attributes.description: Predicted functional consequence of the SNP on gene function as annotated by the variant annotation pipeline (e.g., missense_variant, synonymous_variant, intron_variant, 3_prime_UTR_variant, stop_gained). Uses Sequence Ontology (SO) terms as standardized by Ensembl VEP and ANNOVAR. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: missense_variant|synonymous_variant|intron_variant|3_prime_UTR_variant|stop_gained|splice_region_variant|intergenic_variant|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Sequence Ontology (SO); Ensembl Variant Effect Predictor (VEP); ANNOVAR; ClinVar

attributes.name: genotype_call
attributes.description: The diploid genotype call at this locus expressed as allele1/allele2 (e.g., A/A, A/G, G/G) using VCF-compatible notation. Represents the observed allelic state of the sample at this SNP position. Null indicates a no-call.

attributes.name: genotype_class
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the genotype call: homozygous_ref (both alleles match reference), heterozygous (one REF, one ALT allele), homozygous_alt (both alleles are ALT), or no_call (insufficient data for a confident call). Used for GWAS, pharmacogenomics stratification, and ancestry analysis.

attributes.name: genotype_posterior_probability
attributes.description: The posterior probability of the reported genotype call, expressed as a decimal between 0 and 1. Derived from Bayesian genotype likelihood models (e.g., BEAGLE imputation, array intensity clustering). Higher values indicate greater statistical confidence in the call. Used for imputation quality filtering.
attributes.references: VCF Specification v4.3 (GA4GH/hts-specs); BEAGLE Imputation Software; GA4GH

attributes.name: genotype_quality_score
attributes.description: Phred-scaled genotype quality score (GQ) representing the confidence in the genotype call, analogous to the Phred Score used in sequencing. Higher values indicate greater confidence. Typically ranges 0–99 for array-based calls and 0–99+ for sequencing-based calls. Used for call filtering and QC thresholding.
attributes.references: VCF Specification v4.3 (GA4GH/hts-specs); Phred Quality Score Standard; ISO 15189

attributes.name: genotyping_method
attributes.description: The technology or assay method used to generate this SNP genotype call. Values: array (SNP microarray), wgs (Whole Genome Sequencing), wes (Whole Exome Sequencing), targeted_panel (targeted sequencing panel), qpcr (quantitative PCR-based genotyping), other. Drives downstream analytical workflow selection and QC thresholds.
attributes.references: ISO 15189; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA IVD Guidance

attributes.name: gwas_catalog_trait
attributes.description: The disease or phenotypic trait associated with this SNP as catalogued in the NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog (e.g., type 2 diabetes, breast cancer, LDL cholesterol). Null if no GWAS association is recorded. Enables phenotype-driven SNP filtering and reporting for research and clinical genomics applications.
attributes.references: NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog; NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy; EFO Ontology

attributes.name: haplotype_block_identifier
attributes.description: Identifier for the linkage disequilibrium (LD) haplotype block in which this SNP resides, as defined by the reference haplotype panel. Used for haplotype-based pharmacogenomics star allele calling (e.g., CYP2D6, CYP2C19), ancestry inference, and LD-aware GWAS analysis.
attributes.references: PharmGKB Haplotype Nomenclature; CPIC Pharmacogenomics Guidelines; HapMap Project

attributes.name: hardy_weinberg_p_value
attributes.description: P-value from the Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium (HWE) exact test for this SNP locus within the study population. Significant deviation from HWE (e.g., p < 1e-6) may indicate genotyping error, population stratification, or selection pressure. A standard QC metric in GWAS and population genomics workflows.
attributes.references: GWAS QC Best Practices (Anderson et al.); GWAS Catalog Standards; NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy

attributes.name: imputation_r2_score
attributes.description: The imputation quality metric (R2 or INFO score) for imputed SNP calls, representing the estimated squared correlation between imputed and true genotypes. Ranges 0–1; values below threshold (e.g., <0.3) indicate poor imputation quality. Null for directly genotyped variants. Standard metric from MINIMAC/BEAGLE imputation tools.
attributes.references: MINIMAC4 Imputation Software; BEAGLE; GWAS Catalog Imputation Standards

attributes.name: is_imputed
attributes.description: Indicates whether this SNP genotype call was statistically imputed (True) rather than directly measured by the assay (False). Imputed calls are inferred from haplotype reference panels (e.g., 1000 Genomes, TOPMed) and carry additional uncertainty. Critical for distinguishing directly genotyped from imputed variants in downstream analyses.
attributes.references: GWAS Catalog Imputation Standards; TOPMed Imputation Server; GA4GH

attributes.name: minor_allele_frequency
attributes.description: The frequency of the less common allele at this SNP locus within the study cohort or population, expressed as a decimal between 0 and 0.5. A critical QC and analytical metric for GWAS, population stratification, and pharmacogenomics studies. SNPs with MAF below threshold (e.g., <0.01) may be excluded from association analyses.
attributes.references: GWAS Catalog Standards; gnomAD Population Frequency Database; NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy

attributes.name: pharmacogenomics_phenotype
attributes.description: The pharmacogenomics metabolizer or response phenotype associated with this SNP genotype call (e.g., poor_metabolizer, intermediate_metabolizer, normal_metabolizer, ultrarapid_metabolizer for CYP450 genes). Derived from CPIC or PharmGKB guidelines. Null for non-pharmacogenomics SNPs. Supports precision medicine drug dosing applications.
attributes.references: CPIC Pharmacogenomics Guidelines; PharmGKB; FDA Table of Pharmacogenomic Biomarkers

attributes.name: position
attributes.description: 1-based genomic coordinate (base pair position) of the SNP locus on the reference chromosome. Used for positional queries, regional filtering, linkage disequilibrium analysis, and integration with annotation databases such as ClinVar and gnomAD.
attributes.references: GA4GH Variant Representation Specification; UCSC Genome Browser; Ensembl

attributes.name: probe_identifier
attributes.description: The array probe or bead identifier used to interrogate this SNP locus in array-based genotyping platforms (e.g., Illumina SNP array probe ID). Null for sequencing-based genotyping. Enables traceability to the physical array design, probe performance metrics, and manifest file.
attributes.references: Illumina Array Manifest Specification; Illumina BaseSpace Sequence Hub

attributes.name: reference_allele
attributes.description: The reference allele nucleotide sequence at this locus as defined by the reference genome assembly (e.g., GRCh38). Stored in IUPAC nucleotide notation. Required for genotype interpretation, variant effect prediction, and VCF-format compatibility.
attributes.references: VCF Specification v4.3 (GA4GH/hts-specs); NCBI dbSNP; GRCh38 Reference Assembly

attributes.name: reference_genome_assembly
attributes.description: The reference genome assembly version used for alignment and coordinate assignment of this SNP locus (e.g., GRCh38, GRCh37/hg19). Critical for genomic coordinate interpretation, cross-study harmonization, and liftover operations. Positions are assembly-specific and must not be compared across assemblies without liftover.
attributes.references: NCBI Genome Reference Consortium; Ensembl; GA4GH Reference Genome Standards

attributes.name: result_status
attributes.description: Lifecycle status of this SNP genotype result record: preliminary (initial call pending review), final (reviewed and released), amended (corrected after final release), cancelled (result voided), failed_qc (result failed Quality Control thresholds and is excluded from analysis). Governs data release and downstream consumption eligibility.
attributes.references: HL7 FHIR DiagnosticReport Status; ISO 15189; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; FDA 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: review_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when a qualified scientist or clinical reviewer approved or amended this genotype result, transitioning it to final or amended status. Null for preliminary or failed_qc results. Required for GxP audit trail and CLIA/CAP laboratory compliance.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; GxP Data Integrity Guidelines; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493; CAP Accreditation Standards

attributes.name: reviewed_by
attributes.description: Identifier of the scientist, bioinformatician, or clinical laboratory director who reviewed and approved this genotype result. Stored as an employee or user identifier string. Required for GxP electronic signature compliance and CLIA/CAP laboratory director accountability.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 Electronic Records; GxP Data Integrity Guidelines; CLIA 42 CFR Part 493

attributes.name: rs_number
attributes.description: NCBI dbSNP reference SNP cluster identifier (rsID) for the variant locus. Provides a globally standardized identifier for the SNP, enabling cross-study comparisons, GWAS catalog lookups, pharmacogenomics database queries, and ancestry panel alignment. Example: rs429358.
attributes.references: NCBI dbSNP; NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy; GA4GH Variant Representation Specification

attributes.name: source_file_name
attributes.description: The name of the source data file (e.g., VCF, FASTQ, IDAT, GTC) from which this SNP genotype result was extracted during pipeline processing. Supports data lineage tracing from the Silver Layer record back to the raw data file in the Bronze Layer or instrument output. Examples: sample001.vcf.gz, sample001.idat.
attributes.references: VCF Specification v4.3 (GA4GH/hts-specs); Illumina IDAT Format; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; GxP Data Integrity

attributes.name: strand
attributes.description: The DNA strand orientation of the SNP locus relative to the reference genome: forward (+) or reverse (-). Required for correct allele interpretation in array-based genotyping where probe strand orientation affects allele assignment, and for cross-platform harmonization.
attributes.references: Illumina Array Manifest Specification; UCSC Genome Browser Strand Convention

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this SNP genotype result record was last modified (e.g., status change, amendment, QC flag update). Serves as the RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED timestamp. Used for incremental data pipeline processing and change data capture.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; GxP Data Integrity Guidelines; ISO 27001; SOX

attributes.name: variant_filter_status
attributes.description: Quality Control (QC) filter status for this SNP genotype result, analogous to the FILTER field in VCF format. PASS indicates the locus passed all QC thresholds. Filtered values indicate the specific QC criterion that failed (low quality score, low call rate, low MAF, Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium deviation, strand bias). Used to exclude low-quality calls from downstream analyses. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: PASS|filtered_low_quality|filtered_low_call_rate|filtered_low_maf|filtered_hwe|filtered_strand_bias|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: VCF Specification v4.3 (GA4GH/hts-specs); GWAS QC Best Practices; ISO 15189

products.name: artifact_tag_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the metadata tagging relationship between genomic artifacts and catalog tags. It captures the assignment of controlled vocabulary tags to genomic data assets for discovery, access control, compliance reporting, and FAIR principle alignment. Each record links one genomic artifact to one catalog tag with assignment metadata including who tagged, when, confidence score, approval status, and effective dates.. Existence Justification: In genomics bioinformatics operations, genomic artifacts (FASTQ, BAM, VCF files) receive multiple catalog tags for discovery, access control, and compliance (e.g., WGS, clinical-grade, PHI, FAIR-compliant). Each artifact has many tags, and each tag applies to many artifacts. The business actively manages these tag assignments with approval workflows, confidence scoring, effective dates, and audit trails. This is operational metadata management, not analytical correlation.

products.name: pipeline_authorization
products.description: This association product represents the contractual authorization and validation agreement between a specific pipeline version and a customer account. It captures customer-specific validation status, approved usage scope, effective dates per customer contract, and customer-specific parameter overrides that exist only in the context of this relationship. Each record links one pipeline_version to one account with regulatory and contractual attributes governing how that customer may use that specific pipeline version.. Existence Justification: In genomics biotechnology operations, multiple customer accounts use the same validated pipeline versions (e.g., a standard DRAGEN germline pipeline used by 50+ clinical labs for their respective patient cohorts), AND each customer account uses multiple pipeline versions (e.g., a biopharma partner uses germline, somatic, RNA-seq, and CNV pipelines across different research programs). The relationship represents a contractual and regulatory authorization that the business actively manages with customer-specific validation status, approved usage scope, effective dates per customer contract, and customer-specific parameter overrides.

attributes.name: authorization_notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes capturing special conditions, restrictions, or context for this customer-pipeline authorization. Examples: customer-specific validation protocol references, usage restrictions, or renewal conditions.

attributes.description: JSON-serialized configuration document capturing customer-specific parameter overrides or constraints for this pipeline version. attributes.description: Minimum sequencing read depth required for confident variant calling in this assay version. Expressed as number of reads covering a genomic position. Critical QC (Quality Control) parameter for NGS (Next-Generation Sequencing) assays.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence

attributes.name: minimum_phred_score
attributes.description: Minimum base quality score (Phred score) threshold for variant calling. Higher scores indicate higher confidence in base calls. Typical clinical thresholds are Q30 or higher.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this assay version record was last updated. Tracks configuration changes and supports change control processes.

attributes.name: multiplexing_strategy
attributes.description: Strategy used for pooling multiple samples in a single sequencing run. Single index uses one barcode; dual index uses two barcodes for higher sample throughput and reduced index hopping.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence

attributes.name: panel_gene_list_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the curated gene list or panel used in this assay configuration. Tracks which genes are included in targeted sequencing or array-based assays. Essential for clinical validity documentation.

attributes.name: retired_date
attributes.description: Date when this assay version was retired from active clinical use. Null if the version is still active or planned. Critical for traceability of which version was used for historical patient results.

attributes.name: sensitivity_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of true positive results correctly identified by the assay (true positives divided by true positives plus false negatives). Key analytical performance metric for clinical validity.

attributes.name: sequencing_platform
attributes.description: Type of sequencing instrument or platform used for this assay version (e.g., Illumina NovaSeq, Illumina MiSeq, Ion Torrent). Platform-specific parameters affect data quality and analysis pipelines.

attributes.name: specificity_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of true negative results correctly identified by the assay (true negatives divided by true negatives plus false positives). Key analytical performance metric for clinical validity.

attributes.name: target_read_length
attributes.description: Target length of sequencing reads in base pairs for this assay version. Affects ability to detect structural variants and map reads to repetitive regions.

attributes.name: test_classification
attributes.description: Regulatory classification of the test: IVD (In Vitro Diagnostic) for FDA-cleared or CE-marked tests, LDT (Laboratory Developed Test) for CLIA-validated tests, or RUO (Research Use Only) for non-clinical tests.
attributes.references: FDA U.S. Food and Drug Administration

attributes.name: turnaround_time_hours
attributes.description: Target time from sample receipt to report delivery for this assay version, measured in hours. Used for SLA (Service Level Agreement) tracking and operational planning.

attributes.name: variant_calling_algorithm
attributes.description: Name and version of the primary variant calling algorithm used in this assay version (e.g., GATK HaplotypeCaller, FreeBayes, VarScan). Algorithm choice affects sensitivity and specificity of variant detection.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence

attributes.name: version_number
attributes.description: Semantic version number of the clinical assay configuration (e.g., 1.0, 2.1, 3.0.1). Follows semantic versioning convention to track major and minor changes.

attributes.name: version_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of this assay version. Draft indicates under development; validation indicates undergoing analytical validation; active indicates approved for clinical use; deprecated indicates superseded but still in use; retired indicates no longer in use; withdrawn indicates removed from catalog due to regulatory or quality issues.

attributes.description: Name or identifier of the clinical facility, hospital, or physician office where the specimen was collected. Used for quality tracking and logistics analysis.

attributes.name: collection_site_clia_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Collection Site Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) Number
attributes.description: CLIA certification number of the collection site if applicable. Required for regulatory compliance when collection site is a certified laboratory.

attributes.name: collection_time
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the specimen was collected from the patient. Used for time-sensitive pre-analytical quality assessments and cfDNA stability calculations.

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text comments or notes regarding specimen collection, handling, quality, or special circumstances. Used for communication between laboratory staff and for audit documentation.

attributes.name: consent_date
attributes.description: Date when patient consent was obtained for genomic testing. Used for audit trails and regulatory compliance verification.
attributes.references: IRB - Institutional Review Board; GDPR; HIPAA

attributes.name: consent_obtained
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether informed consent was obtained from the patient for genomic testing and data use. Required for compliance with IRB protocols and GDPR.
attributes.references: IRB - Institutional Review Board; GDPR; HIPAA

attributes.name: container_type
attributes.description: Type of collection container or tube used for specimen transport. Examples: EDTA tube, PAXgene tube, Streck tube, OMNIgene tube, formalin jar. Impacts pre-analytical quality and DNA/RNA stability.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this specimen record was first created in the LIMS. Used for audit trails and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: Date after which the specimen is no longer suitable for testing due to degradation or stability limits. Based on specimen type, storage conditions, and assay requirements.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this specimen record was last modified in the LIMS. Used for audit trails and change tracking.

attributes.name: ordering_physician_name
attributes.description: Full name of the physician or healthcare provider who ordered the genomic test. Used for result reporting and clinical consultation.

attributes.name: ordering_physician_npi
attributes.description: National Provider Identifier (NPI) of the ordering physician. 10-digit unique identifier for healthcare providers in the United States. Required for billing and regulatory reporting.

attributes.name: preanalytical_qc_status
attributes.description: Overall pre-analytical quality control assessment status. Indicates whether specimen meets quality thresholds for downstream testing (Phred Score, DIN, RIN, hemolysis, clotting).

attributes.name: quantity_received
attributes.description: Quantity of specimen received by the laboratory. May differ from collected volume due to aliquoting or partial submission. Unit depends on specimen type (ml for liquid, mg for tissue).

attributes.name: quantity_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the specimen quantity. Varies by specimen type: ml for blood/saliva, mg for tissue, ug for extracted DNA/RNA, cells for cell suspensions, slides for FFPE.

attributes.name: received_date
attributes.description: Date when the specimen was received and accessioned by the clinical laboratory. Start point for laboratory TAT calculations.

attributes.name: received_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the specimen was received and logged into the LIMS. Used for chain-of-custody documentation and pre-analytical time tracking.

attributes.name: rejection_reason
attributes.description: Reason for specimen rejection if QC failed or specimen was deemed unsuitable for testing. Examples: insufficient volume, hemolyzed, mislabeled, expired transport time. Null if specimen was accepted.

attributes.name: source_anatomical_site
attributes.description: Anatomical site or body location from which the specimen was collected. Examples: peripheral blood, bone marrow, lung tissue, colon biopsy. Critical for pathology correlation and variant interpretation.

attributes.name: specimen_status
attributes.description: Current state of the specimen in the clinical laboratory workflow. Tracks progression from receipt through testing to final disposition.
attributes.references: CAP - College of American Pathologists; ISO 15189

attributes.name: specimen_type
attributes.description: Type of biological specimen collected for genomic testing. Defines the material source for DNA/RNA extraction and sequencing.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 - Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence; CLIA

attributes.name: storage_condition
attributes.description: Current storage temperature and condition for the specimen. Critical for maintaining specimen integrity and meeting pre-analytical quality requirements.

attributes.name: storage_location
attributes.description: Physical storage location identifier within the laboratory (freezer ID, shelf, box, position). Used for specimen retrieval and inventory management.

attributes.name: volume_collected_ml
attributes.description: Volume of specimen collected in milliliters. Critical for determining sufficiency for testing and for calculating input quantities for library preparation.

products.name: analytical_validation
products.description: Records the analytical performance validation data for each clinical assay version — including LOD (Limit of Detection), analytical sensitivity, analytical specificity, precision (repeatability/reproducibility), accuracy, linearity, interference studies, and reference range establishment. Captures validation study design, number of replicates, acceptance criteria, pass/fail determination, validation date, and approving scientist. Required for CLIA/CAP accreditation and FDA/EMA regulatory submissions.

attributes.name: analytical_validation_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the analytical validation record. Primary key for the analytical validation entity.

attributes.name: analytical_report_document_controlled_document_id
attributes.description: Reference to the controlled document containing the final validation study report with all results, analysis, and conclusions. Required for regulatory submissions and accreditation inspections.

attributes.name: assay_development_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to research.assay_development. Business justification: Analytical validation studies validate specific assay development efforts. Required for regulatory submissions (510(k), PMA, LDT notifications), CLIA complexity determination, and CAP accreditation. L

attributes.name: catalog_item_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.catalog_item. Business justification: Validation studies are product-specific; catalog linkage essential for regulatory submissions (FDA 510k, IVDR technical files), product specification documentation, and lifecycle management. Critical

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the qualified scientist or laboratory director who reviewed and approved the validation study. Must be a CLIA-qualified high-complexity testing director or equivalent.

attributes.name: genome_assembly_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.genome_assembly. Business justification: Analytical validation studies must document reference genome used for performance characterization. Required for FDA/CAP regulatory submissions and assay version control. Enables tracking validation s

attributes.name: internal_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.internal_order. Business justification: Validation studies are tracked as internal orders for cost accumulation, budget control, and settlement to fixed assets when capitalization criteria are met. Enables project-based accounting for valid

attributes.name: ivd_test_catalog_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical assay being validated. Links this validation study to the specific assay version under evaluation.

attributes.name: primary_analytical_controlled_document_id
attributes.description: Reference to the controlled document containing the detailed validation study protocol. Links to document management system for version control and audit trail.

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_id
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the FDA 510(k), PMA, or EMA submission that includes this validation data. Links validation records to regulatory approval documentation.
attributes.references: FDA In Vitro Diagnostic Device Guidance

attributes.name: validation_study_id
attributes.description: Business identifier for the validation study protocol. Used for cross-referencing with study design documents and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: CAP College of American Pathologists Laboratory Accreditation

attributes.name: acceptance_criteria
attributes.description: Pre-defined performance thresholds that the assay must meet to pass validation. Includes specific numeric criteria for sensitivity, specificity, precision, accuracy, and other performance metrics.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence

attributes.name: accuracy_bias
attributes.description: Systematic deviation of assay results from the true or reference value, expressed as a percentage. Positive bias indicates overestimation; negative bias indicates underestimation.
attributes.references: CLSI Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute EP09 Guidelines

attributes.name: analytical_sensitivity
attributes.description: Proportion of true positive results correctly identified by the assay, expressed as a percentage. Measures the assay's ability to detect the target analyte when present.
attributes.references: FDA In Vitro Diagnostic Device Guidance

attributes.name: analytical_specificity
attributes.description: Proportion of true negative results correctly identified by the assay, expressed as a percentage. Measures the assay's ability to correctly identify samples without the target analyte.
attributes.references: FDA In Vitro Diagnostic Device Guidance

attributes.name: approving_scientist_name
attributes.description: Full name of the qualified scientist or laboratory director who approved the validation study. Required for regulatory documentation and audit trails.
attributes.references: CAP College of American Pathologists Laboratory Accreditation

attributes.name: comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, observations, deviations from protocol, or special considerations identified during the validation study. Used for capturing context not covered by structured fields.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this validation record was first created in the system. Part of the audit trail for data governance and compliance.

attributes.name: intended_use
attributes.description: Regulatory classification of the assay. IVD (In Vitro Diagnostic) for FDA-cleared tests; RUO (Research Use Only) for non-clinical applications; LDT (Laboratory Developed Test) for CLIA-validated in-house assays.
attributes.references: FDA In Vitro Diagnostic Device Guidance

attributes.name: interference_result
attributes.description: Overall determination of whether tested substances interfere with assay performance. No interference indicates acceptable performance; interference detected requires mitigation or sample rejection criteria; conditionally acceptable indicates interference only at extreme concentrations.
attributes.references: CLSI Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute EP07 Guidelines

attributes.name: interference_substances_tested
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of endogenous and exogenous substances evaluated for potential interference with assay performance. Common interferents include hemoglobin, lipids, bilirubin, and common medications.
attributes.references: CLSI Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute EP07 Guidelines

attributes.name: linearity_r_squared
attributes.description: Coefficient of determination for the linearity study regression analysis. Values closer to 1.0 indicate stronger linear relationship. Typical acceptance criterion is R² ≥ 0.95.
attributes.references: CLSI Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute EP06 Guidelines

attributes.name: linearity_range_lower
attributes.description: Lower boundary of the concentration range over which the assay demonstrates a linear relationship between input and output. Defines the minimum reportable value.
attributes.references: CLSI Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute EP06 Guidelines

attributes.name: linearity_range_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for the linearity range boundaries. Must be consistent with LOD unit and assay measurement unit.
attributes.references: CLSI Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute EP06 Guidelines

attributes.name: linearity_range_upper
attributes.description: Upper boundary of the concentration range over which the assay demonstrates a linear relationship between input and output. Defines the maximum reportable value before dilution is required.
attributes.references: CLSI Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute EP06 Guidelines

attributes.name: lod_unit
attributes.business_glossary_term: Limit of Detection (LOD) Unit of Measure
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for the LOD value. Common units include ng/mL, copies/mL, percentage, or variant allele frequency depending on assay type.
attributes.references: CLSI Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute EP17 Guidelines

attributes.name: lod_value
attributes.description: Lowest concentration or quantity of analyte that can be reliably detected by the assay. Critical performance metric for regulatory approval and clinical interpretation.
attributes.references: CLSI Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute EP17 Guidelines

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this validation record was last modified. Tracks changes for audit trail and data lineage purposes.

attributes.name: pass_fail_determination
attributes.description: Final determination of whether the assay met all acceptance criteria. Pass indicates full approval for clinical use; fail requires remediation; conditional pass indicates approval with specific limitations or monitoring requirements.
attributes.references: CAP College of American Pathologists Laboratory Accreditation

attributes.name: precision_repeatability
attributes.description: Coefficient of variation for within-run precision, expressed as a percentage. Measures consistency of results when the same sample is tested multiple times under identical conditions by the same operator.
attributes.references: CLSI Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute EP05 Guidelines

attributes.name: precision_reproducibility
attributes.description: Coefficient of variation for between-run precision, expressed as a percentage. Measures consistency of results across different runs, days, operators, and reagent lots.
attributes.references: CLSI Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute EP05 Guidelines

attributes.name: reference_population_description
attributes.description: Demographic and clinical characteristics of the population used to establish the reference range. Includes age range, sex distribution, ethnicity, and health status criteria.
attributes.references: CLSI Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute EP28 Guidelines

attributes.name: reference_range_lower
attributes.description: Lower boundary of the normal or expected range for the analyte in the reference population. Used for clinical interpretation of patient results.
attributes.references: CLSI Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute EP28 Guidelines

attributes.name: reference_range_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for the reference range boundaries. Must be consistent with assay reporting unit.
attributes.references: CLSI Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute EP28 Guidelines

attributes.name: reference_range_upper
attributes.description: Upper boundary of the normal or expected range for the analyte in the reference population. Used for clinical interpretation of patient results.
attributes.references: CLSI Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute EP28 Guidelines

attributes.name: replicate_count
attributes.description: Number of replicate measurements performed for each sample in the validation study. Higher replicate counts improve precision estimates.
attributes.references: CLSI Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute EP05 Guidelines

attributes.name: sample_size
attributes.description: Total number of samples or replicates tested in the validation study. Adequate sample size is critical for statistical power and regulatory acceptance.
attributes.references: FDA In Vitro Diagnostic Device Guidance

attributes.name: validation_approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the validation study was formally approved by the laboratory director or quality assurance team. Authorizes the assay for clinical use or regulatory submission.

attributes.name: validation_completion_date
attributes.description: Date when all validation testing was completed and results were finalized. Marks the end of the experimental phase before review and approval.

attributes.name: validation_start_date
attributes.description: Date when the validation study was initiated. Used for tracking study duration and regulatory submission timelines.

attributes.name: validation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the validation study. Tracks progression from planning through execution to final approval or failure determination.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence

attributes.name: validation_type
attributes.description: Category of validation study performed. Initial validation establishes performance characteristics; revalidation confirms continued performance after changes; verification confirms manufacturer claims; method comparison evaluates against reference methods; bridging validates changes to existing validated assays.

Core clinical output entity.
