attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: CLIA accreditation fees, inspection preparation costs, and PT program expenses are charged to laboratory operations cost centers. Link enables regulatory compliance budget tracking, cost allocation fo

attributes.name: laboratory_director_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: CLIA regulations mandate designated laboratory director who must be qualified internal employee. Critical for regulatory compliance, inspection readiness, personnel qualification tracking, and linking

attributes.name: accreditation_fee_amount_usd
attributes.description: The total fee amount paid or due for the accreditation or certificate, expressed in US dollars. Includes application fees, inspection fees, and annual maintenance fees.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.638 Fee for Determination of Program Compliance, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program Fee Schedule

attributes.name: accreditation_fee_payment_status
attributes.description: Current status of payment for accreditation fees. Tracks whether fees have been paid, are pending, or are overdue, which may impact accreditation standing.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.638 Fee for Determination of Program Compliance, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program Fee Schedule

attributes.name: accreditation_scope
attributes.description: Detailed description of the scope of testing authorized under this accreditation. Includes test categories, specialty areas, complexity levels (waived, moderate, high), and specific analytes or methodologies covered.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.5 Categorization of Tests, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program Checklist

attributes.name: accreditation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the accreditation. Indicates whether the laboratory is currently authorized to perform clinical testing under this accreditation.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.1806 Suspension, Limitation, or Revocation of Certificate, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program

attributes.name: certificate_number
attributes.description: The externally-issued unique certificate or accreditation number assigned by CLIA or CAP. Business identifier for the accreditation agreement.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.1 Certificate Requirements, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program

attributes.name: certificate_type
attributes.description: Classification of the accreditation or certificate type. Indicates the regulatory framework and scope of laboratory operations permitted.
attributes.value_regex: CLIA Certificate of Waiver|CLIA Certificate of Compliance|CLIA Certificate of Accreditation|CAP Accreditation|State License
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.1 Certificate Types, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program

attributes.name: complexity_level
attributes.description: The CLIA complexity categorization of tests authorized under this accreditation. Determines regulatory requirements for personnel, quality control, and proficiency testing.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.5 Categorization of Tests by Complexity

attributes.name: corrective_action_due_date
attributes.description: The deadline by which corrective action plans must be submitted or implemented to address inspection deficiencies. Nullable if no corrective action is required.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.1806 Enforcement Actions, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program Corrective Action Requirements

attributes.name: corrective_action_status
attributes.description: Current status of corrective action plans submitted in response to inspection deficiencies. Tracks the laboratory's progress in addressing compliance gaps.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.1806 Enforcement Actions, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program Corrective Action Requirements

attributes.name: created_by_user
attributes.description: The username or identifier of the user who created this accreditation record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this accreditation record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: deficiencies_cited_count
attributes.description: The total number of deficiencies or non-conformances identified during the most recent inspection. Used to assess compliance risk and prioritize corrective actions.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.1806 Enforcement Actions, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program Inspection Report

attributes.name: deficiency_summary
attributes.description: Narrative summary of the deficiencies or non-conformances cited during the most recent inspection. Includes checklist item references, severity classification, and areas requiring corrective action.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.1806 Enforcement Actions, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program Inspection Report

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which the accreditation or certificate became valid and the laboratory was authorized to begin or continue clinical testing operations under this credential.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.1 Certificate Requirements, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: The date on which the accreditation or certificate expires and must be renewed. Nullable for indefinite or rolling accreditations pending inspection cycles.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.1 Certificate Requirements, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program

attributes.name: inspection_outcome
attributes.description: The overall result or finding from the most recent inspection. Indicates whether the laboratory met all requirements, had minor recommendations, or had deficiencies requiring corrective action.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.1806 Enforcement Actions, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program Inspection Report

attributes.name: issuing_body
attributes.description: The regulatory or accrediting organization that issued the certificate. Examples include CMS (Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services), CAP (College of American Pathologists), state health departments, or other approved accrediting organizations.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.551 Approved Accreditation Organizations, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program

attributes.name: laboratory_address
attributes.description: The physical address of the clinical laboratory facility. Required for regulatory reporting, inspection scheduling, and certificate issuance. Organizational contact data classified as confidential.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.1 Certificate Requirements, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program

attributes.name: laboratory_clia_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Laboratory Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) Number
attributes.description: The unique 10-digit CLIA identification number assigned to the laboratory by CMS. This is the primary regulatory identifier for the laboratory and is distinct from the certificate number.

attributes.name: laboratory_name
attributes.description: The official name of the clinical laboratory holding this accreditation. Used for regulatory reporting, certificate display, and external communications.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.1 Certificate Requirements, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: The date of the most recent on-site inspection or survey conducted by the accrediting body or regulatory agency. Critical for tracking compliance cycles and renewal timelines.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.1773 Inspection Frequency, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program Inspection Schedule

attributes.name: last_modified_by_user
attributes.description: The username or identifier of the user who last modified this accreditation record. Used for audit trail and accountability.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this accreditation record was last updated or modified. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and data quality monitoring.

attributes.name: next_inspection_due_date
attributes.description: The scheduled or anticipated date for the next on-site inspection or survey. Used for proactive compliance planning and resource allocation.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.1773 Inspection Frequency, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program Inspection Schedule

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, comments, or context related to the accreditation record. May include special conditions, historical context, or internal tracking information.

attributes.name: pt_analyte_test_system
attributes.business_glossary_term: Proficiency Testing (PT) Analyte or Test System
attributes.description: The specific analyte, test system, or specialty area evaluated through proficiency testing. Examples include Glucose, HbA1c, Molecular Oncology, Cytogenetics, or specific gene panels.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.801 Proficiency Testing Requirements, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program PT Requirements

attributes.name: pt_corrective_action_required_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Proficiency Testing (PT) Corrective Action Required Flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether corrective action is required in response to unsuccessful proficiency testing performance. True indicates corrective action is required; False indicates acceptable performance.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.855 Unsuccessful Proficiency Testing Performance, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program PT Corrective Action

attributes.name: pt_enrollment_period
attributes.description: The time period or cycle for which the laboratory is enrolled in the proficiency testing program. Typically expressed as a year or year-quarter (e.g., 2024-Q1, 2024 Annual).
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.801 Proficiency Testing Requirements, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program PT Requirements

attributes.name: pt_graded_outcome
attributes.description: The overall graded outcome or performance result for the proficiency testing cycle. Indicates whether the laboratory met acceptable performance criteria for the analyte or test system.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.823 Proficiency Testing Performance Standards, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program PT Grading

attributes.name: pt_program_name
attributes.description: The name of the proficiency testing program in which the laboratory is enrolled. Examples include CAP Surveys, ARUP Proficiency Testing, or other CMS-approved PT providers.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.801 Proficiency Testing Requirements, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program PT Requirements

attributes.name: pt_results_submitted_count
attributes.description: The number of proficiency testing results or reports submitted by the laboratory during the enrollment period. Used to verify compliance with PT submission requirements.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.801 Proficiency Testing Requirements, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program PT Requirements

attributes.name: pt_sample_sets_received
attributes.description: The number of proficiency testing sample sets or challenges received by the laboratory during the enrollment period. Used to track PT participation completeness.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.801 Proficiency Testing Requirements, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program PT Requirements

attributes.name: pt_score_percent
attributes.description: The percentage score achieved by the laboratory on the proficiency testing challenge. Calculated as the number of acceptable results divided by the total number of challenges, expressed as a percentage.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.823 Proficiency Testing Performance Standards, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program PT Grading

attributes.name: pt_submission_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the laboratory submitted proficiency testing results by the required deadline. True indicates on-time submission; False indicates late or missing submission.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.801 Proficiency Testing Requirements, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program PT Requirements

attributes.name: pt_submission_deadline
attributes.description: The deadline by which proficiency testing results must be submitted to the PT provider. Used to track compliance with PT submission timelines and avoid late submission penalties.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.801 Proficiency Testing Requirements, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program PT Requirements

attributes.name: renewal_application_date
attributes.description: The date on which the laboratory submitted the renewal application for the accreditation or certificate. Used to track renewal cycle timelines and compliance with submission deadlines.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.1 Certificate Requirements, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program Renewal Process

attributes.name: renewal_workflow_status
attributes.description: Current status of the accreditation renewal process. Tracks the laboratory's progress through the renewal application, review, and approval workflow.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.1 Certificate Requirements, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program Renewal Process

attributes.name: test_specialty_areas
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of specialty areas or disciplines covered by the accreditation (e.g., Molecular Pathology, Cytogenetics, Clinical Chemistry, Hematology, Microbiology). Defines the breadth of clinical testing capabilities.
attributes.references: CLIA 42 CFR 493.1441 Specialty and Subspecialty Requirements, CAP Laboratory Accreditation Program

products.name: clinical_consent_record
products.description: PHI-compliant record of patient informed consent for clinical genomic testing — capturing consent type (germline testing, somatic testing, research use, biobanking, return of incidental findings), consent version, consent date, method of consent (written/electronic), patient or guardian signature reference, IRB protocol number, withdrawal status, and withdrawal date. Required for HIPAA compliance, GDPR data subject rights, and NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy adherence.

attributes.name: clinical_consent_record_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the clinical consent record. Primary key for tracking patient consent throughout the clinical genomics workflow.

attributes.name: account_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to customer.account. Business justification: Clinical labs track institutional account affiliations for consent management in research collaborations and IRB protocol compliance. Required for institutional consent reporting, HIPAA business assoc

attributes.name: consent_form_controlled_document_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Consent Form Controlled Document Id (Foreign Key)
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.controlled_document. Business justification: Consent records must reference the specific IRB-approved consent form version used. Regulatory requirement for human subjects research (45 CFR 46) and clinical testing (CLIA/CAP). Critical for audit t

attributes.name: dpia_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to data.dpia. Business justification: Consent records are inputs to DPIA assessments - they define the legal basis and scope of data processing. Demonstrating lawful basis for processing under GDPR requires linking consent records to the

attributes.name: genomic_access_control_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to data.genomic_access_control. Business justification: Consent records define access control policies - what data can be used for what purposes based on patient consent scope. Consent-driven data governance requires linking consent to the access control p

attributes.name: irb_submission_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to research.irb_submission. Business justification: Consent records must link to specific IRB submissions for audit trails, protocol version compliance, continuing review documentation, and regulatory inspections (FDA, OHRP). Required for human subject

attributes.name: patient_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier linking this consent record to the patient in the clinical system. Required for PHI-compliant consent tracking.

attributes.name: rd_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to research.project. Business justification: Consent records link to research projects for data use authorization tracking, HIPAA compliance, research participant enrollment verification, and project-level consent reporting. Essential for resear

attributes.name: submission_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.submission. Business justification: Research consent records link to regulatory submissions (IND, IDE, 510k validation studies) when patient samples are used for regulatory evidence generation. Required for IRB compliance and FDA audit

attributes.name: audit_trail_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier to the detailed audit trail log for this consent record. Required for 21 CFR Part 11 compliance and regulatory inspections.

attributes.name: biobanking_permitted_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether patient consented to long-term storage of biological samples for future research or testing. Required for biorepository management.

attributes.name: consent_date
attributes.description: Date when the patient provided informed consent. Used to determine consent validity period and regulatory compliance timelines.

attributes.name: consent_document_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the consent document. Used for audit trails and regulatory submissions.

attributes.name: consent_expiration_date
attributes.description: Date when the consent expires and must be renewed. Null for consents without expiration. Required for time-limited research protocols.

attributes.name: consent_language
attributes.description: ISO 639-3 three-letter language code indicating the language in which consent was obtained. Required for multilingual patient populations and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: consent_location
attributes.description: Physical or virtual location where consent was obtained (clinic name, hospital, telehealth platform). Required for audit trails and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: consent_method
attributes.description: Method by which consent was obtained from the patient or legal guardian. Determines documentation and audit requirements.

attributes.name: consent_scope_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of what the patient consented to, including specific tests, data usage, and sharing permissions. Required for informed consent documentation.

attributes.name: consent_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the consent record. Determines whether genomic testing and data usage are permissible.

attributes.name: consent_type
attributes.description: Category of consent provided by the patient. Determines scope of permissible genomic testing and data usage.

attributes.name: consent_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the consent form template used. Required for tracking consent form changes over time and ensuring regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: consenting_party_name
attributes.description: Full legal name of the individual who provided consent. Required for legal documentation and audit trails.

attributes.name: consenting_party_type
attributes.description: Relationship of the person providing consent to the patient. Required for minors, incapacitated patients, or legally authorized representatives.

attributes.name: consenting_physician_name
attributes.description: Name of the physician or healthcare provider who obtained informed consent from the patient. Required for clinical accountability and audit trails.

attributes.name: consenting_physician_npi
attributes.description: National Provider Identifier of the physician who obtained consent. Required for regulatory reporting and provider accountability.

attributes.name: created_by_user
attributes.description: User identifier of the person who created this consent record. Required for accountability and audit trails.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this consent record was first created in the system. Required for audit trails and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: data_sharing_permitted_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether patient consented to sharing of de-identified genomic data with external databases or research consortia. Required for NIH and GDPR compliance.

attributes.name: gdpr_compliant_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) Compliant Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this consent record meets GDPR requirements for EU patients. Required for international genomic testing operations.

attributes.name: germline_testing_permitted_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether patient consented to germline genomic testing (inherited variants). Critical for test ordering and result interpretation.

attributes.name: incidental_findings_return_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether patient consented to receive incidental or secondary findings from genomic testing. Required per ACMG guidelines for return of results.

attributes.name: interpreter_used_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a medical interpreter was used during the consent process. Required for documenting informed consent quality and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: irb_approval_date
attributes.description: Date when the IRB approved the consent form and protocol. Used to validate consent form currency and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: irb_protocol_number
attributes.description: IRB protocol number under which this consent was obtained. Required for research use and clinical trial genomic testing.

attributes.name: last_modified_by_user
attributes.description: User identifier of the person who last modified this consent record. Required for accountability and change tracking.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this consent record was last modified. Required for audit trails and change tracking.

attributes.name: phi_compliant_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this consent record meets all HIPAA PHI protection requirements. Used for compliance audits and data governance.

attributes.name: recontact_permitted_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether patient consented to be recontacted for future research opportunities or updated findings. Required for longitudinal genomic studies.

attributes.name: regulatory_jurisdiction
attributes.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code indicating the regulatory jurisdiction governing this consent. Required for multi-country genomic testing operations.

attributes.name: research_use_permitted_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether patient consented to use of genomic data for research purposes beyond clinical care. Required for NIH data sharing compliance.

attributes.name: signature_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier to the stored signature artifact (electronic or scanned paper). Used for audit and legal verification purposes.

attributes.name: somatic_testing_permitted_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether patient consented to somatic genomic testing (tumor/acquired variants). Required for oncology genomic testing workflows.

attributes.name: withdrawal_date
attributes.description: Date when patient withdrew consent. Null if consent has not been withdrawn. Required for GDPR right to withdraw and HIPAA compliance.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 7 Right to Withdraw Consent

attributes.name: withdrawal_method
attributes.description: Method by which patient communicated withdrawal of consent. Required for audit trail and regulatory compliance. Null if consent not withdrawn.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 7 Right to Withdraw Consent

attributes.name: withdrawal_reason
attributes.description: Free-text explanation of why patient withdrew consent. Used for quality improvement and regulatory reporting. Null if consent not withdrawn.
attributes.references: GDPR Article 7 Right to Withdraw Consent

attributes.name: witness_name
attributes.description: Full name of the witness who observed the consent process. Required for certain consent types and regulatory jurisdictions. Null if witness not required.

attributes.name: witness_signature_reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier to the stored witness signature artifact. Required for certain consent types. Null if witness not required.

products.name: assay_qc_run
products.description: Quality control run record for a clinical assay batch or sequencing run — capturing QC run ID, assay version, run date, instrument ID, reagent lot numbers, control sample results (positive, negative, no-template), QC metrics (coverage uniformity, on-target rate, duplicate rate, mean coverage depth, contamination check), Westgard rule evaluation, pass/fail determination per acceptance criteria, and reviewing scientist sign-off. Supports CLIA QC documentation, Westgard multi-rule monitoring, and lot release decisions. Links failed QC runs to CAPA workflows.
products.reference: Assay QC Run / Laboratory QC Record

attributes.name: assay_qc_run_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the quality control run record. Primary key for the assay QC run entity.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 - Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence

attributes.name: approval_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to regulatory.regulatory_approval. Business justification: QC runs validate assay performance within specifications established in the regulatory approval (LOD, sensitivity, specificity). Required for demonstrating continued compliance with approval condition

attributes.name: asset_id
attributes.description: Reference to the sequencing instrument or analysis platform on which the QC run was performed. Critical for instrument-specific performance tracking and calibration.

attributes.name: bioinformatics_pipeline_run_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to bioinformatics.pipeline_run. Business justification: Assay QC runs validate clinical test performance using bioinformatics pipeline outputs (positive/negative controls, coverage metrics, contamination checks). Links QC metrics to the pipeline execution

attributes.name: catalog_item_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to product.catalog_item. Business justification: QC runs validate specific commercial test products; catalog linkage required for lot release decisions, regulatory submissions (validation reports), and product-specific quality metrics tracking per C

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: QC runs consume reagents, controls, and labor charged to laboratory operations cost centers. Link enables cost-per-test analysis, operational budgeting, and variance analysis between planned and actua

attributes.name: deviation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to quality.quality_deviation. Business justification: QC run failures (coverage depth, contamination, control failures, Westgard rule violations) are the primary source of quality deviations in clinical genomics labs. Must link for root cause analysis, C

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the qualified laboratory scientist who reviewed and approved the QC run results. Required for CLIA compliance and CAP accreditation.

attributes.name: flow_cell_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the flow cell used in the sequencing run. Tracks consumable lot-level performance and enables traceability for NGS quality issues.

attributes.name: genome_assembly_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reference.genome_assembly. Business justification: QC metrics (coverage depth, on-target rate) are reference-genome-dependent. Required for lot release documentation, trending analysis, and troubleshooting QC failures. Links QC runs to specific refere

attributes.name: ivd_test_catalog_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: In Vitro Diagnostic (IVD) Test Catalog Identifier
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical test catalog entry for which this QC run was performed. Links to the specific assay version and test definition.
attributes.references: IVDR - EU In Vitro Diagnostic Regulation 2017/746

attributes.name: primary_assay_sample_specimen_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the positive control sample included in the QC run. Used to verify assay sensitivity and detect false negatives.

attributes.name: production_batch_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to manufacturing.production_batch. Business justification: QC runs consume reagent batches; lot-to-lot performance tracking required for release decisions and trending analysis. Replaces denormalized reagent_lot_number with proper FK for batch genealogy and s

attributes.name: qc_material_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.material. Business justification: QC runs validate specific reagent materials/lots before clinical use; material-level tracking enables lot release decisions, regulatory compliance (CLIA/CAP), and investigation of QC failures linked t

attributes.name: reagent_lot_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to reagent.lot. Business justification: Clinical QC runs must trace to specific reagent lots (library prep kits, sequencing reagents) for regulatory compliance, lot release decisions, and root cause analysis when QC failures occur. Critical

attributes.name: sequencing_run_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to sequencing.sequencing_run. Business justification: Clinical assay QC runs validate sequencing run quality for diagnostic use. Regulatory requirement for CLIA/CAP compliance - QC controls must be traceable to the sequencing run they validate. Essential

attributes.name: acceptance_criteria_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the acceptance criteria document used to evaluate this QC run. Ensures traceability to validated QC thresholds.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 - Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence

attributes.name: capa_initiated_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Initiated Flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether a CAPA workflow was initiated as a result of this QC run failure or out-of-specification result.

attributes.name: capa_reference_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Reference Number
attributes.description: Reference number linking this QC run to the associated CAPA record in the quality management system. Enables traceability of quality issues to resolution.

attributes.name: cluster_density
attributes.description: Number of clusters per square millimeter on the flow cell. Optimal density ensures adequate signal intensity without overcrowding that degrades quality.

attributes.name: contamination_check_percent
attributes.description: Estimated percentage of cross-sample contamination detected through allele frequency analysis or sample fingerprinting. Values above threshold trigger QC failure.

attributes.name: coverage_uniformity_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of target bases covered at a uniform depth, indicating consistency of sequencing across the target region. Low uniformity may indicate technical issues.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 - Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence

attributes.name: created_by_user
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the laboratory personnel who created this QC run record. Part of the audit trail required for CLIA and CAP compliance.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this QC run record was first created in the laboratory information management system.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 - Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence

attributes.name: duplicate_rate_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of sequencing reads identified as PCR or optical duplicates. High duplicate rates reduce effective coverage and may indicate library complexity issues.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 - Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence

attributes.name: error_rate_percent
attributes.description: Estimated sequencing error rate based on PhiX control or known reference sequences. Monitors instrument and reagent performance over time.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 - Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence

attributes.name: failure_reason
attributes.description: Detailed explanation of why the QC run failed, including which metrics or controls did not meet acceptance criteria. Used for root cause analysis and CAPA.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 - Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence

attributes.name: last_modified_by_user
attributes.description: Username or identifier of the laboratory personnel who last modified this QC run record. Maintains complete audit trail for regulatory inspections.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this QC run record was last updated. Supports audit trail and change tracking for regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 - Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence

attributes.name: library_prep_kit_lot
attributes.description: Lot number of the library preparation kit used for sample processing prior to sequencing. Tracks consumable quality impact on QC metrics.

attributes.name: lot_release_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this QC run supports lot release decisions for reagents or consumables. Used in manufacturing quality control workflows.

attributes.name: mean_coverage_depth
attributes.description: Average number of sequencing reads covering each base position across the target region. Key metric for assessing sequencing quality and variant calling confidence.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 - Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence

attributes.name: negative_control_result
attributes.description: Pass/fail determination for the negative control sample. Failure indicates potential contamination or specificity issues.
attributes.references: CAP - College of American Pathologists Laboratory Accreditation

attributes.name: no_template_control_result
attributes.description: Pass/fail determination for the no-template control. Detects reagent contamination or carryover from previous runs.

attributes.name: on_target_rate_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of sequencing reads that align to the intended target regions. Low on-target rates indicate library preparation or capture efficiency issues.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 - Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence

attributes.name: positive_control_result
attributes.description: Pass/fail determination for the positive control sample. Failure indicates potential assay sensitivity issues requiring investigation.
attributes.references: CAP - College of American Pathologists Laboratory Accreditation

attributes.name: q30_score_percent
attributes.description: Percentage of bases with Phred quality score of 30 or higher, indicating base call accuracy of 99.9% or better. Industry standard metric for sequencing quality.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 - Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence

attributes.name: qc_run_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the QC run, typically formatted as a human-readable run number used in laboratory documentation and CLIA compliance records.

attributes.name: qc_status
attributes.description: Overall pass/fail determination for the QC run based on acceptance criteria evaluation. Determines whether patient samples from this run can be reported.

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this QC run data is included in regulatory submissions to FDA, EMA, or other governing bodies for assay validation or post-market surveillance.
attributes.references: FDA - U.S. Food and Drug Administration

attributes.name: review_comments
attributes.description: Free-text comments from the reviewing scientist documenting observations, conditional pass justifications, or follow-up actions required.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 - Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence

attributes.name: review_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the reviewing scientist completed their evaluation and signed off on the QC run. Establishes audit trail for regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: CAP - College of American Pathologists Laboratory Accreditation

attributes.name: run_completion_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the QC run completed all processing steps and generated final metrics.
attributes.references: CAP - College of American Pathologists Laboratory Accreditation

attributes.name: run_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the QC run was executed in the clinical laboratory.
attributes.references: ISO 15189 - Medical Laboratories Quality and Competence

attributes.name: run_start_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise timestamp when the QC run was initiated on the sequencing instrument or analysis platform.
attributes.references: CAP - College of American Pathologists Laboratory Accreditation

attributes.name: westgard_rule_evaluation
attributes.description: Result of Westgard multi-rule statistical QC evaluation applied to control samples. Documents which Westgard rules (1-2s, 1-3s, 2-2s, R-4s, 4-1s, 10x) were triggered, if any.

products.name: incidental_finding
products.description: Records clinically significant incidental (secondary) findings identified during genomic testing that are outside the primary test indication — capturing finding type (ACMG SF v3.2 gene list, pharmacogenomic, carrier status), variant details, ACMG classification, patient notification preference (per consent), reporting decision (report/not report), reporting date, and genetic counselor assignment. Supports ACMG secondary findings policy compliance and patient communication workflows.

attributes.name: acmg_classification
attributes.business_glossary_term: American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) Variant Classification
attributes.description: ACMG/AMP variant classification tier indicating clinical significance. Pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants are medically actionable.

attributes.name: allele_frequency
attributes.description: Population allele frequency of this variant in reference databases such as gnomAD. Expressed as a decimal between 0 and 1.

attributes.name: alternate_allele
attributes.description: Alternate allele sequence observed in the patient sample at the variant position.

attributes.name: associated_condition
attributes.description: Medical condition or disease associated with this incidental finding. Examples include hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome, Lynch syndrome, familial hypercholesterolemia.

attributes.name: chromosome
attributes.description: Chromosome on which the variant is located. Values include 1-22, X, Y, or MT (mitochondrial).

attributes.name: clinical_action_recommended
attributes.description: Free-text description of recommended clinical actions based on this incidental finding, such as enhanced surveillance, prophylactic interventions, or specialist referral.

attributes.name: clinical_significance
attributes.description: Free-text description of the clinical significance of the incidental finding, including associated disease risk, penetrance, and recommended clinical actions.

attributes.name: clinvar_accession
attributes.description: ClinVar accession number for this variant if the variant has been submitted to ClinVar. Format is VCV followed by numeric identifier.

attributes.name: coverage_depth
attributes.description: Number of sequencing reads covering the variant position. Higher coverage provides greater confidence in variant calling.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this incidental finding record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: dbsnp_accession
attributes.business_glossary_term: Database of Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms (dbSNP) Identifier (ID)
attributes.description: dbSNP reference SNP cluster ID (rsID) for this variant if available. Format is rs followed by numeric identifier.

attributes.name: evidence_summary
attributes.description: Summary of clinical and scientific evidence supporting the variant classification, including references to published literature, functional studies, and population data.

attributes.name: family_cascade_recommended
attributes.description: Indicates whether cascade testing of at-risk family members is recommended based on the clinical significance and inheritance pattern of this finding.

attributes.name: filter_status
attributes.description: Quality filter status applied during variant calling. PASS indicates the variant passed all quality filters; other values indicate specific quality concerns.

attributes.name: finding_type
attributes.description: Category of incidental finding identified. ACMG secondary finding refers to medically actionable genes per ACMG SF v3.2 list; pharmacogenomic refers to drug-gene interactions; carrier status refers to recessive disease alleles.
attributes.references: ACMG Secondary Findings v3.2 Policy Statement

attributes.name: genomic_position
attributes.description: Genomic coordinate (base pair position) of the variant on the reference genome build.

attributes.name: identified_date
attributes.description: Date on which the incidental finding was first identified during bioinformatics analysis or variant interpretation.

attributes.name: interpretation_status
attributes.description: Current status of the variant interpretation workflow for this incidental finding. Draft indicates initial interpretation; reviewed indicates peer review complete; approved indicates sign-out by laboratory director; amended indicates post-release update.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this incidental finding record was last modified, including updates to interpretation status, reporting decision, or variant classification.

attributes.name: patient_consent_preference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Patient Consent Preference for Incidental Findings
attributes.description: Patient preference for receiving incidental findings as documented in informed consent. Receive all indicates patient wants all secondary findings; receive actionable only limits to medically actionable findings; decline all indicates patient opted out.
attributes.references: ACMG Policy on Secondary Findings; 21 CFR Part 50 Informed Consent

attributes.name: patient_notification_date
attributes.description: Date on which the patient was notified of the incidental finding, typically through genetic counseling session or clinical consultation. Null if patient has not yet been notified.
attributes.references: ACMG Policy on Return of Secondary Findings

attributes.name: phi_compliant_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this incidental finding record has been reviewed for HIPAA PHI compliance and appropriate access controls have been applied.

attributes.name: quality_score
attributes.description: Phred-scaled quality score for the variant call. Higher scores indicate greater confidence in the variant call.

attributes.name: reference_allele
attributes.description: Reference allele sequence at the variant position as defined by the reference genome.

attributes.name: reference_genome_build
attributes.description: Human reference genome assembly version used for variant calling and coordinate mapping. GRCh37 (hg19) and GRCh38 (hg38) are the most common builds.

attributes.name: reported_date
attributes.description: Date on which the incidental finding was reported to the patient and ordering physician. Null if reporting decision is do not report.

attributes.name: reporting_decision
attributes.description: Decision on whether to report this incidental finding to the patient and ordering physician. Based on patient consent preference, clinical significance, and laboratory policy.
attributes.references: ACMG Secondary Findings Policy; CLIA 42 CFR 493.1291

attributes.name: reporting_rationale
attributes.description: Free-text explanation of the rationale for the reporting decision, including consideration of patient consent, clinical actionability, and laboratory policy.

attributes.name: variant_allele_fraction
attributes.description: Fraction of sequencing reads supporting the alternate allele at the variant position. Expected to be approximately 0.5 for heterozygous germline variants and 1.0 for homozygous variants.

attributes.name: variant_hgvs_notation
attributes.business_glossary_term: Human Genome Variation Society (HGVS) Variant Notation
attributes.description: Standardized HGVS nomenclature describing the genomic variant associated with this incidental finding. Format follows HGVS guidelines for genomic, coding, or protein-level notation.

attributes.name: zygosity
attributes.description: Zygosity status of the variant. Heterozygous indicates one copy of the variant allele; homozygous indicates two copies; hemizygous applies to X-linked variants in males.

products.name: genetic_counseling_session

Supports ACMG secondary findings policy compliance, precision medicine workflows, and patient-centered care documentation.

products.name: clinical_enrollment
products.description: This association product represents the enrollment event between a clinical patient and a research project. It captures the operational relationship when a patient consents to participate in an R&D study, tracking enrollment lifecycle, consent versions, cohort assignments, and withdrawal events. Each record links one patient to one research project with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific enrollment relationship. Required for IRB reporting, enrollment tracking, and data use authorization compliance.. Existence Justification: In genomics biotech clinical research operations, patients participate in multiple R&D projects over time (longitudinal cohorts, multi-protocol enrollment for different genomic studies), and research projects enroll multiple patients as study participants. The business actively manages Research Enrollment as an operational entity - research coordinators and principal investigators create enrollment records, track consent versions, assign patients to cohorts/randomization arms, monitor enrollment status, and report withdrawals to IRBs. This is not an analytical correlation but a core operational process with dedicated workflows in clinical trial management systems.

products.name: test_service_agreement
products.description: This association product represents the contractual agreement between a clinical test catalog entry and a customer account. It captures account-specific pricing, service level commitments, volume discount tiers, and specimen handling preferences negotiated for each test-account combination. Each record links one test catalog entry to one account with contract terms that exist only in the context of this commercial relationship.. Existence Justification: In genomics biotechnology commercial operations, clinical laboratories and institutional customers negotiate account-specific pricing, service level agreements, and operational terms for each test offered. A single test catalog entry (e.g., WGS Oncology Panel v2.1) is contracted to hundreds of customer accounts with varying negotiated prices, volume discount tiers, TAT commitments, and specimen preferences. Conversely, each customer account contracts for multiple tests from the catalog with distinct terms per test. The business actively manages these test service agreements as contractual entities with lifecycle states (draft, active, renewal), and commercial teams query 'show me all contracted tests for Account X' and 'show me all accounts contracted for Test Y'.

products.name: orderer_authorization
products.description: This association product represents the authorization relationship between authorized orderers (physicians, genetic counselors) and institutional service agreements. It captures the specific ordering privileges, test menu access scope, and authorization terms that exist when a physician is credentialed to order tests under a particular customer service agreement. Each record links one authorized orderer to one service agreement with authorization-specific attributes including authorization dates, status, test menu access scope, ordering limits, and expiration dates. This is a critical compliance and operational entity — physicians may hold ordering privileges under multiple institutional agreements (multi-site affiliations, hospital network memberships), and each service agreement authorizes multiple physicians based on institutional credentialing.. Existence Justification: In genomics biotech clinical operations, physicians frequently hold ordering privileges under multiple institutional service agreements due to multi-site hospital affiliations, academic medical center networks, and participation in evaluation/beta programs. Conversely, each institutional service agreement (hospital system contract, research institution agreement) authorizes multiple physicians based on institutional credentialing rosters. The authorization relationship itself carries critical operational data: authorization dates, status (active/suspended/expired), test menu access scope specific to that agreement, monthly ordering limits for evaluation programs, and authorization expiry dates that may differ from both the physician's general credentialing and the service agreement's term.

products.name: orderer_territory_assignment
products.description: This association product represents the commercial territory assignment relationship between authorized clinical orderers and sales territories. It captures the operational reality that ordering physicians may practice across multiple geographic locations (each covered by different territories) and territories contain many authorized orderers. Each record links one authorized orderer to one territory with assignment dates, coverage type (primary/secondary), and relationship strength metrics used for account planning and sales resource allocation.. Existence Justification: In genomics biotech commercial operations, authorized ordering physicians frequently practice at multiple locations that span different sales territories (e.g., an academic physician with hospital affiliations in 3 cities, each covered by different territory managers). Simultaneously, each territory contains many authorized orderers. The business actively manages these assignments to determine account ownership, allocate sales resources, and track relationship strength for pipeline planning and quota assignment.

products.name: account_hierarchy
products.description: Defines parent-child relationships within customer account structures — enterprise biopharma groups with subsidiary labs, hospital networks with satellite clinical genomics sites, academic consortia with member institutions, and OEM partner trees. Captures parent account, child account, hierarchy level, relationship type (subsidiary, affiliate, consortium member, OEM reseller), effective date, and expiry date. Enables consolidated commercial reporting and volume-based pricing aggregation across account families.

attributes.name: account_hierarchy_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the account hierarchy relationship record.

attributes.name: child_account_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the child account in the hierarchy. References the downstream account such as subsidiary labs, satellite clinical genomics sites, or member institutions.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the user who approved this account hierarchy relationship. References the user management system for accountability and audit trail purposes.

attributes.name: parent_account_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the parent account in the hierarchy. References the upstream account in enterprise structures such as biopharma groups, hospital networks, or academic consortia.

attributes.name: approved_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this account hierarchy relationship was formally approved by sales operations or finance for activation in consolidated reporting and pricing programs. Null for relationships pending approval.

attributes.name: billing_rollup_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether invoices for the child account should be consolidated and rolled up to the parent account for centralized billing. True for enterprise agreements with consolidated invoicing; false for independent billing.

attributes.name: business_segment
attributes.description: Business segment classification for this hierarchical relationship, indicating the primary market focus. Enables segment-specific reporting and strategic analysis across RUO (Research Use Only), IVD (In Vitro Diagnostic), and other genomics applications.

attributes.name: consolidation_eligible_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this hierarchical relationship qualifies for consolidated commercial reporting and volume-based pricing aggregation. True for relationships that should roll up revenue, orders, and usage; false for informational-only links.

attributes.name: contract_reference_number
attributes.description: Reference number of the master service agreement, enterprise contract, or consortium agreement that governs this hierarchical relationship. Links to contract management systems for terms and conditions.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this account hierarchy relationship record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: Date when the hierarchical relationship becomes active and begins participating in consolidated commercial reporting and pricing aggregation. Supports temporal queries and historical analysis.

attributes.name: expiry_date
attributes.description: Date when the hierarchical relationship ends or is scheduled to terminate. Null for open-ended relationships. Enables time-bound hierarchy analysis and future-state planning.

attributes.name: geographic_region
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the primary geographic region where this hierarchical relationship operates. Used for regional sales reporting and compliance segmentation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: USA|CAN|GBR|DEU|FRA|CHN|JPN|AUS|IND|BRA|MEX|ITA|ESP|NLD|CHE|SWE|SGP|KOR|ISR|BEL — 20 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: hierarchy_level
attributes.description: Numeric level in the account hierarchy tree structure. Level 1 represents the top-level parent, with increasing numbers for deeper nested relationships. Enables depth-based queries and rollup aggregations.

attributes.name: hierarchy_path
attributes.description: Materialized path representation of the full account hierarchy from root to current node, typically formatted as slash-delimited account identifiers (e.g., /1001/2045/3078/). Enables efficient ancestor and descendant queries without recursive joins.

attributes.name: legal_entity_code
attributes.description: Code identifying the legal entity or company code under which this hierarchical relationship is registered for financial and regulatory reporting purposes. Aligns with ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) company code structures.
attributes.references: SAP S/4HANA FI Company Code Structure

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this account hierarchy relationship record was last modified. Tracks the most recent update for change management and audit purposes.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional free-text notes or comments about this account hierarchy relationship, capturing special instructions, historical context, or operational considerations for sales and finance teams.

attributes.name: ownership_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage of ownership or control the parent account holds over the child account. Used for financial consolidation, revenue attribution, and equity-based reporting. Null for non-ownership relationships such as consortium members or OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) resellers.

attributes.name: pricing_tier_inheritance_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the child account inherits volume-based pricing tiers and discounts from the parent account. True for subsidiaries and affiliates participating in enterprise pricing programs; false for independent pricing.

attributes.name: primary_hierarchy_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this is the primary hierarchical relationship for the child account. True when this parent-child link is the authoritative path for reporting and aggregation; false for secondary or alternate hierarchies.

attributes.name: relationship_description
attributes.description: Free-text description providing additional context about the hierarchical relationship, such as the business rationale, legal structure details, or special commercial arrangements between parent and child accounts.

attributes.name: relationship_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the hierarchical relationship. Active relationships participate in volume-based pricing and consolidated reporting; inactive or terminated relationships are excluded.

attributes.name: relationship_type
attributes.description: Classification of the hierarchical relationship between parent and child accounts. Defines the legal, operational, or commercial nature of the connection for consolidated reporting and pricing aggregation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: subsidiary|affiliate|consortium_member|oem_reseller|branch|division|franchise — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: salesforce_account_hierarchy_code
attributes.description: External identifier from Salesforce CRM (Customer Relationship Management) system representing this account hierarchy relationship. Enables traceability to the source system of record for customer master data.

products.name: segment
products.description: Market segmentation classification applied to customer accounts for commercial targeting, pricing strategy, and service tiering. Segments include RUO (Research Use Only), IVD/clinical, biopharma drug development, agricultural genomics, OEM/reseller, and academic/government. Stores segment code, segment name, regulatory use classification (RUO vs. IVD), market vertical, sub-vertical, strategic tier (key account, growth, standard), assigned pricing tier, SLA tier, and segment owner. Drives downstream product eligibility, promotional eligibility, and support prioritization.

attributes.name: segment_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the customer segment classification record. Primary key.

attributes.name: active_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this segment is currently active and in use for customer classification (True) or has been retired/deprecated (False).

attributes.name: consent_requirement_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether accounts in this segment require explicit consent management for data processing and marketing communications (True) or operate under standard terms (False). Relevant for GDPR and HIPAA compliance.

attributes.name: contract_term_months
attributes.description: Standard contract duration in months for accounts in this segment (e.g., 12 for annual contracts, 36 for multi-year agreements). Null if no standard term applies.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this segment record was first created in the system. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: credit_limit_usd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Standard Credit Limit in United States Dollars (USD)
attributes.description: Standard credit limit assigned to accounts in this segment for credit risk management. Expressed in USD. Null if no standard limit applies.

attributes.name: effective_end_date
attributes.description: Date when this segment classification was retired or superseded. Null if currently active. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

attributes.name: effective_start_date
attributes.description: Date when this segment classification became effective and available for customer assignment. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.

attributes.name: geographic_scope
attributes.description: Primary geographic scope or region where this segment operates (e.g., GLOBAL for worldwide segments, USA for US-only, EMEA for Europe/Middle East/Africa). attributes.name: gxp_compliance_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether accounts in this segment operate under GxP regulations (GMP, GLP, GCP) and require validated systems, audit trails, and regulatory documentation (True) or not (False).
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11, ICH Q7, ISO 13485

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this segment record was last updated. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.

attributes.name: market_sub_vertical
attributes.description: More granular sub-classification within the market vertical (e.g., Oncology Research, Rare Disease Diagnostics, Crop Genomics, Companion Diagnostics).

attributes.name: market_vertical

attributes.name: owner_email

attributes.name: owner_name
attributes.description: Name of the business leader or product manager responsible for this segment strategy and performance (e.g., VP of Clinical Markets, Director of Academic Sales).

attributes.name: payment_terms_days
attributes.description: Standard payment terms in days for accounts in this segment (e.g., 30 for Net 30, 60 for Net 60). Drives accounts receivable and credit management.

attributes.name: phi_handling_required_flag
attributes.business_glossary_term: Protected Health Information (PHI) Handling Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether accounts in this segment handle Protected Health Information (PHI) and require HIPAA-compliant data handling, Business Associate Agreements (BAA), and enhanced security controls (True) or not (False).

attributes.name: preferred_sales_channel
attributes.description: Primary sales channel used to serve accounts in this segment (e.g., DIRECT for direct sales force, DISTRIBUTOR for channel partners, ONLINE for e-commerce).

attributes.name: pricing_tier
attributes.description: Pricing tier assigned to this segment, determining discount levels, volume pricing eligibility, and contract terms. Drives product pricing and promotional eligibility.

attributes.name: product_eligibility_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this segment has access to the full product catalog (True) or restricted product eligibility based on regulatory or commercial constraints (False).

attributes.name: promotional_eligibility_flag

attributes.name: regulatory_use_classification
attributes.description: Primary regulatory classification of the segment: RUO (Research Use Only), IVD (In Vitro Diagnostic), LDT (Laboratory Developed Test), CLINICAL (clinical use), RESEARCH (research only), or MIXED (multiple use cases).

attributes.name: segment_code
attributes.description: Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the segment (e.g., RUO_ACADEMIC, IVD_CLINICAL, BIOPHARMA_DRUG_DEV). Used as business key for segment classification.

attributes.name: segment_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the segment characteristics, target customer profile, and business rationale for this segmentation.

attributes.name: segment_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the customer segment (e.g., Research Use Only - Academic Institutions, In Vitro Diagnostic - Clinical Laboratories).

attributes.name: sla_tier
attributes.description: Service level agreement tier defining support response times, technical assistance levels, and service prioritization (e.g., PREMIUM for 24/7 support, STANDARD for business hours).

attributes.name: source_system
attributes.description: System of record where this segment definition originated (e.g., SALESFORCE_CRM for CRM-managed segments, SAP_SD for ERP-managed segments, MANUAL for manually defined segments).

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Unique identifier of this segment record in the source system (e.g., Salesforce Record ID, SAP segment code). Used for data lineage and reconciliation.

attributes.name: strategic_tier
attributes.description: Strategic importance classification of accounts in this segment: KEY_ACCOUNT (top-tier strategic partners), STRATEGIC (high-value established), GROWTH (high-potential expansion), STANDARD (regular commercial), EMERGING (new/developing).

attributes.name: support_priority_level
attributes.description: Numeric priority level for technical support and field application scientist assistance (1=highest priority, 5=standard priority). Drives support queue prioritization.

attributes.name: target_annual_revenue_usd

attributes.description: Target annual revenue contribution from all accounts in this segment. Used for segment performance tracking and strategic planning. Expressed in USD.

attributes.name: target_asp_usd
